produced_reading: Heavy cloth application — cloth applied with heavy pressure/coverage. 'cl' = cloth (from our tool shorthand), 'hv' = heavy (from our modifier list: hv=heavy).

Warm cloth — cloth that has been warmed before application. 'cl' = cloth, 'w' = warm (parallel to 'cl-c' = cool cloth, 'cl-w' = warm cloth). Discussed in postmortem as a proposed shorthand but never confirmed as needed since no warm-cloth procedures were encountered.

Cloth applied with firm pressure/coverage. 'cl' = cloth, 'fm' = firm (from our modifier list: fm=firm). Interpretable but never negotiated as a compound form — firmness was written out inline (e.g. 'cl 2 adj edges L fm 10s').
Cloth applied with light pressure/coverage. 'cl' = cloth, 'lt' = light (from our modifier list: lt=light). Interpretable by analogy but never negotiated as a compound form.

Cloth at normal/ambient temperature — neither cooled nor warmed. 'cl' = cloth, 'n' = normal. Proposed in postmortem discussion as part of a temperature trio (cl-c, cl-w, cl-n) but never formally confirmed or used in live rounds.

Fan producing cool air. 'fn' = fan (from our tool shorthand), 'c' = cool. This is the critical discovery from Round 9: fan must be described as producing cool air to work correctly. Proposed in postmortem as shorthand for cool-air fan.

Fan producing warm air. 'fn' = fan, 'w' = warm. Discussed in postmortem as a theoretical possibility ('could fan air ever be warm/hot?'), but the engineer explicitly confirmed no warm-air fan procedures exist in the stellar table. Never used.
Fan producing ambient (room-temperature) air. 'fn' = fan, 'a' = ambient. Proposed in postmortem as a counterpart to 'fn-c', to distinguish cool vs ambient airflow.
